text:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: GPU queue depth > 95% for cluster-prod-gpu in us-west-2. Autoscaler failed to attach new nodes. Pager duty: @oncall assigned.

pagerduty: Incident triggered (P1) — gpu-queue-growth. First alert at 2026-04-01T03:46:32Z.

emma: seeing spike in inference queue, latency up from 90ms -> 1.2s, errors 502 on some customer routes.

raj: logs show repeated autoscaler join failures: "attachrole propagation timeout" and launchtemplate mismatch warnings.

carla: confirmed customer-facing impact: 3 paying tenants reporting degraded response times, metrics show token backlog increasing. Sending bridge to CSM.

simone: grabbed the runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-capacity — step 1 is to check ASG/NodeGroup health and last launch events.

dmitri: running quick query against cluster events:
```
kubectl get nodes -o wide --selector=redwood/gpu=true
kubectl describe nodegroup ng-gpu-prod | tail -n 50
```

dmitri: output shows multiple nodes in Pending for >6m, attach role status: "InstanceProfile not associated yet" and taint apply failing for taint=redwood:gpu.

emma: autoscaler logs (trimmed):
```
E0401 03:48:10 autoscaler.go:412] failed to scale up: failed to register node: Join failed: iam:PassRoleDenied
E0401 03:48:14 autoscaler.go:415] launchTemplate mismatch: expected ami-0abcd got ami-0ef01
E0401 03:48:16 autoscaler.go:419] taint application error: node not ready -> skipping
```

raj: IAM errors suggest EC2 instances unable to assume instance profile, maybe propagation lag after a recent change. Who touched the NG IAM role?

carla: I rolled a small patch to the NG instance profile yesterday to add S3 permissions for logging bucket (ticket RW-1142). It completed, but AWS console shows role update at 2026-04-01T00:22Z.

simone: possible timeline: role updated -> instance profile rotation -> propagation to new instances lagging -> autoscaler failing to attach role -> nodes stuck in provisioning -> taints not applied -> scheduler backlog.

ops-bot: Suggest manual warm-provision as stopgap. Admins can launch a GPU instance from the working LT/AMI and attach it to the nodegroup until autoscaler recovers.

emma: trying manual bootstrap now. Command: `aws ec2 run-instances --launch-template LaunchTemplateId=lt-0a12 --count 1 --instance-type p4d.24xlarge`

dmitri: hold — before doing that, confirm the correct LT/AMI and instance profile. Current prod LT revision = 7, AMI = ami-0abcd1234 (verified ok). The nodegroup is referencing LT v7 but autoscaler logs claim v6/other AMI for some requests -> possible stale controller cache.

raj: I'm going to force a nodegroup refresh in kube-controller: `eksctl utils update-nodegroup --cluster prod --name ng-gpu-prod --force-refresh` (running now).

carla: launching manual instance with correct profile now to reduce queue: `aws ec2 run-instances --launch-template LaunchTemplateId=lt-0a12 --count 2 --iam-instance-profile Name=rg-prod-gpu`

simone: pinging AWS support internal contact to check instance profile association propagation and any API rate limits on AttachRole.

(3 minutes pass)

ops-bot: paging note — manual instances came up, kubelet registered on one, second stuck with Join failed: timed out. Queue decreased from 9k -> 4.2k tokens. Latency improved to 480ms median. :white_check_mark:

emma: partial mitigation in place, but autoscaler still rejecting new node joins. We should keep the manual bridge until autoscaler stable.

raj: update on eksctl refresh: controller synced, but discovered a drift between launch template versions across the ASG and nodegroup: one ASG was still using LT v6 due to a failed update job during the previous deploy window. That explains the mismatch errors.

dmitri: found further evidence in cloudtrail: repeated `ec2:RunInstances` calls returned `AccessDenied` for the instance profile for 12 of 24 attempts between 03:42–03:50Z.

carla: CSM bridge update: telling customers we have partial mitigation and no data loss, degraded latency for some routes. Notifying impacted teams.

simone: AWS says instance profile propagation delay is expected after role changes; recommended to wait ~10–15m or re-associate the instance profile. They also flagged a high APICalls rate from our autoscaler causing throttling warnings.

dmitri: I see us hitting EC2 API quotas for RunInstances ~spike at 03:44Z. Autoscaler retried rapidly and compounded the issue. Need to add exponential backoff.

emma: action items for immediate mitigation: 1) keep manual instances up until autoscaler stable, 2) throttle autoscaler launch rate (add 30s cooldown), 3) re-associate correct LT to ASG, 4) rollback the instance profile change if propagation not completing.

raj: implementing autoscaler cooldown: flipping feature flag `autoscaler.launch_cooldown=30s` in infra-config and restarting controller. Deploying now.

carla: I can rollback the S3 permission change on the instance profile if needed. Hold until we see if re-association fixes it.

(10 minutes pass)

ops-bot: update: autoscaler cooldown in effect. New run attempts are spaced. EC2 API 5xxs decreased. Nodes starting to successfully attach with correct IAM. Queue steady at 1.1k tokens.

emma: monitoring shows customer error rates back to baseline for 2 tenants, one still seeing spikes. Ticket RW-2196 created for follow-up with infra.

simone: opened AWS case for API rate impact and role propagation timeline. Case ID: AWS-99281.

dmitri: we should document the combined failure mode: role change -> instance profile propagation lag + autoscaler retry storm -> EC2 API quota exhaustion -> join failures -> taint apply delays -> scheduler backlog.

carla: taking ownership of post-incident: will coordinate the rollback or staged reapply of instance profile, add a guard in future role updates (CI job that pauses scales), and write a short playbook for manual warm-provision.

raj: follow-up infra tasks I'm taking: add exponential backoff to autoscaler RunInstances, expose cooldown config in console, and add monitoring alert for EC2 API throttling.

emma: on the customer side I'll follow up with CSM for the impacted tenants and schedule an RC for any service credits if SLA match.

simone: oncall handoff in 30m. @dmitri can you stay for the handoff?

dmitri: yes.

ops-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident status -> mitigated (manual workarounds in place, autoscaler healthy). Will switch to postmortem mode.

carla: notes for postmortem: timeline, root cause hypothesis, mitigation steps taken, customer impact summary, follow-ups (infra, runbook, alerts).

emma: adding a short blameless root-cause summary to RW-INC-2026-04-01 and assigning action owners.

(End of thread)
